chief_complaint: Hypertension with obesity and prediabetes requiring risk factor management
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57‑year‑old woman with a long‑standing history of obesity (onset 1986) and prediabetes (onset 1989). Essential hypertension was diagnosed in July 2018 and is currently treated with hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. Chronic anemia has been documented since 1995. Social factors include persistent social isolation (since 2013), limited social contact (since 1983), prior homelessness resolved in 2018, and low educational attainment (primary school only). She is employed full‑time since 2016. The most recent vital signs (12/14/2018) show SBP 117 mmHg, DBP 95 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension) and an A1c of 6.3 % (prediabetic). No recent lipid panel, renal function, or BMI data are available. The record shows infrequent health‑care encounters, primarily wellness visits, with the last encounter in December 2018.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include acute bronchitis (resolved 2018‑12‑22), viral sinusitis (resolved 2018‑09‑26 and 2016‑06‑22), gingivitis (resolved 2016‑07‑12), prior homelessness (resolved 2018‑06‑14), stress (resolved 2018‑07‑09), medication review due (resolved 2018‑07‑09 and 2017‑07‑03), and a period of not being in the labor force (resolved 2016‑06‑27).
social_determinants: The patient experiences chronic social isolation and limited social contact, has a history of homelessness (resolved), low educational attainment (primary school only), and is employed full‑time. These factors, together with a possible engagement in risk‑related activities, likely influence health‑seeking behavior and disease management.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure: SBP 117 mmHg, DBP 95 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension). Glycemic control: A1c 6.3% (prediabetic). BMI, heart rate, eGFR, total cholesterol, and LDL are missing.
